question: How do advanced software engineering organizations (Google, Microsoft, AWS, Netflix, OpenAI, Anthropic) structure automated software factory governance and agentic execution pipelines?
scope: Software factory mechanisms, CI/CD gates, policy enforcement, reversibility tiers, human-in-the-loop escalation
claims: High-performing software factories decouple plan simulation (dry-run) from physical production execution.
Policy-governed execution reduces human error while preserving safety on high-risk irreversible operations.
evidence: Google SRE release gates prevent unverified code from reaching production.
AWS IAM least-privilege boundary policies prevent unauthorized resource mutation.
observations: Reversibility must inversely govern agent autonomy level: highly reversible actions allow high autonomy, while irreversible actions require explicit human sign-off.
Single-file edits should not trigger heavy multi-agent team composition penalties.
limitations: Hyperscale CI/CD pipelines require adaptation for lightweight local-first execution.
recommendation: Adopt policy-governed execution, reversibility tiers, and task graph governance in EOS Autonomous Engineering Factory.
